title: Cascade Analytics - Open models, context needs, and toolchain discovery
summary: Initial discovery with Cascade Analytics focusing on evaluating open models (Llama/Mistral/Falcon variants), clarifying context-length requirements (8k vs 32k/64k), multilingual QA and tool-calling for data connectors. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (latency, cost, data residency, SOC2/SSO). Agreed next steps: send model perf matrix, security pack, pricing scenarios for Hosted and Dedicated, and schedule a 1-hr technical deep dive POC kickoff.
topics: Open model comparisons (Llama, Mistral, Falcon, quantization tradeoffs)
Context window needs and inference cost implications (8k / 32k / 64k)
Tool/function calling and connectors (DB, internal APIs, embeddings+rerank)
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: security, latency, and cost tradeoffs
POC scope and benchmarks (latency p95, throughput, token cost)
next_steps: Maya to send model performance matrix (Llama/Mistral/Falcon variants) and recommended quant profiles - due 2026-01-03
Jordan to share a short runbook for KV caching and prefix caching options in Redwood - due 2026-01-05
Redwood to provide Hosted vs Dedicated pricing scenarios and estimated monthly cost for 100k QPS-equivalent tokens - due 2026-01-04
Schedule 1-hr POC kickoff (technical deep dive) with Priya and Tom present - target week of 2026-01-12
Customer to send a sample prompt set and business-critical success criteria doc - Priya to own
action_items: Maya: Send model perf matrix and recommended quantization profiles; due 2026-01-03
Jordan: Draft KV/prefix cache runbook and recommended batching settings; due 2026-01-05
Priya: Share sample prompt set and core regen tests; due 2026-01-06

transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-28 14:30 UTC | Duration ~52m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Arjun (Redwood SE), Lena (Cascade CTO), Priya (ML), Tom (Eng), Miguel (PM), Anita (Sec)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time today. Quick intro from Redwood side — I'm Maya, AE, and Jordan and Arjun are our solutions engineers. Could folks on the Cascade side intro briefly?
[00:18] Lena: Sure, I'm Lena, CTO at Cascade. We build analytics pipelines for telco and fintech customers. Priya will lead ML, Tom is infra, Miguel PM, Anita is security.
[00:28] Maya: Awesome. High level today is model selection and deployment options — hosted, dedicated, private — and how that maps to your context window and tool-calling needs. Does that align?
[00:36] Miguel: Yeah, main thing is we want to evaluate open models, and also clarify tradeoffs if we need VPC/on-prem for some regulated customers.
[00:44] Jordan: Great. Maybe start with Priya on model and context needs?
[00:47] Priya: Sure. Our typical use is real-time customer-facing assistants plus batch summarization of call transcripts. The real-time flows need latency sub-300ms ideally p95, and must handle multi-turn doc context — about 10-30k tokens in some cases, so we're exploring 8k vs 32k vs even 64k windows for longer transcripts. Also multilingual — many customers in Latin America so Spanish and Portuguese, sometimes code-switching with English.
[01:11] Jordan: Thanks. On models, are you set on open models only, or is there a mix?
[01:15] Priya: Preference for open due to cost and control, but we need quality parity with OpenAI for summarization and instruction following. We're evaluating Llama derivatives, Mistral, Falcon. Plus we want to test quantized variants to see token cost.
[01:26] Arjun: One thing we've seen — not all 32k-window models are equal. Some models are native 32k, others are window-extended with sliding tricks. Also quantization (4-bit, q4, awq) can change latency and perplexity.
[01:40] Tom: Quick question — on Redwood side where does KV cache live? If we run Dedicated or Private, we want to minimize network hops.
[01:48] Jordan: Good question. KV cache is in-memory on the serving nodes. For Dedicated pools we colocate the model and cache; for Hosted we manage caching and can pin customers to same shard to reduce cross-az latency. Note: sometimes our auto-transcript has term K V cache written weird.
[02:02] Lena: On security, some of our regulated customers require data residency in EU and SOC 2. We also have SAML SSO. Anita here will walk through those.
[02:10] Anita: Yeah, SOC 2 is table stakes; also need audit logs, KMS integration for keys, and an option for private control plane or V P C peering for the most sensitive tenants.
[02:21] Maya: Understood. Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packaging; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and SLA; Hosted is fastest to start but we can discuss customer-managed keys or bring-your-own-key options.
[02:33] Priya: For the model comparisons, what metrics should we expect? Perplexity, ROUGE, latency p50/p95, token cost for a 30k prompt?
[02:42] Jordan: We usually provide a perf matrix: generation latency (p50/p95) across batch sizes, tokens-per-second throughput, quality-on-our eval prompts (we'll run your prompt set), and token cost estimates accounting for quantization and batching. We'll share a sample.
[02:57] Miguel: Tool-calling is super important: we need function or tool calling to call internal microservices — user profile lookup, billing APIs, and sometimes run database queries. How is that supported?
[03:07] Arjun: We support structured tool calling like function call semantics and streaming responses. On Dedicated/Private you can host a small helper in the same VPC to proxy calls to your internal APIs. We also have embeddings+rerank pipelines if you want retrieval augmented generation (RAG) with vector DB.
[03:21] Priya: For retrieval we plan to store embeddings in our vector DB (we currently use Pinecone but open to switching). Any limits on context + retrieved docs? For example we might stitch 15 docs of 1k tokens each.
[03:33] Jordan: Practically the model's context window and your prompt engineering define the cap. We often recommend an RAG pattern with scoring and rerank, and use prefix caching for repeated prompts. If you need to stitch 15x1k that's 15k tokens — need a 32k-capable model or chunk and summarize. Also memory impact on throughput.
[03:50] Tom: On latency — you mentioned p95; how much does batching affect our real-time flows? If we enable batching to reduce cost, will that harm latency?
[03:58] Arjun: There's a trade. Continuous batching reduces per-token cost, but for strict sub-300ms p95 you'd configure small max-batch and fast flush intervals. Dedicate can give you predictable latency because GPUs are reserved. Hosted can be tuned too but under heavy load we might route to a lower-cost pool which can increase variance unless you use Dedicated.
[04:18] Lena: Let's talk numbers — for 100k tokens/day what are the rough Hosted vs Dedicated monthly numbers? Even ballpark.
[04:25] Maya: We'll send detailed pricing scenarios. Ballpark: Hosted will be simpler per-token pricing; Dedicated becomes cost-effective when you hit sustained volume and need lower variance and higher throughput. We'll calculate break-even in the matrix.
[04:36] Priya: For multilingual evaluation, any gotchas? Some models are better at Spanish/Portuguese; some are trained primarily on English.
[04:44] Jordan: Right. Mistral variants tend to generalize, but Llama-derivatives with fine-tuning can be strong. We'll run your Spanish/Portuguese prompt set. Also watch for tokenization differences — some languages expand token count.
[04:58] Miguel: About tool-calling again — do you support step-by-step tool orchestration, like calling multiple tools in a flow?
[05:04] Arjun: Yes; we have patterns for orchestrating multiple tool calls. We surface structured metadata in the response so you can deterministically call downstream services. There's also a function-calling interface compatible with common SDK patterns.
[05:15] Anita: How do we audit who called what? Need an immutable log of requests and tool invocations for compliance.
[05:21] Jordan: We capture request traces, model version, routing decisions, and you can enable longer retention on logs for Dedicated/Private. We also support SSO-based user attribution and exportable audit logs.
[05:34] Priya: Any constraints on model-extensions like 64k windows? We have some long transcripts requiring near-100k context if we include raw audio+metadata.
[05:42] Arjun: Native 64k models exist but are rare; some techniques like Hierarchical RAG, streaming summarization, or external chunking plus progressive summarization work better than trying to push 100k into a single pass. For very long docs we recommend summarization pipelines or storing intermediate representations.
[05:58] Tom: For a POC, what's the minimal infra footprint? Prefer Hosted to start?
[06:03] Maya: Many customers start Hosted to iterate, then move to Dedicated when they need predictable latency or isolation. If your security posture requires VPC and private control plane from day one, we can spin up a Private trial but that takes longer.
[06:15] Lena: Timeboxes: we want a pilot within 3 weeks and a decision in 6–8 weeks. Is that reasonable?
[06:20] Maya: Yes, that's typical. We'll propose a POC scope: run your prompt set across 3 models (one Llama-derivative, Mistral, Falcon), include Spanish/Portuguese tests, evaluate latency and token cost, and test tool-calling.
[06:32] Priya: Good. Also want to test quantized models (4-bit AWQ or q4) to measure quality drop.
[06:38] Jordan: We'll include quantized variants in the perf matrix. Note: quantization can reduce token cost significantly but may increase hallucinations on instruction tasks; we'll report regression metrics on your prompts.
[06:51] Miguel: Any recommended models for call summarization specifically?
[06:54] Arjun: Models fine-tuned for instruction or summarization tend to do better. We can also run a small supervised fine-tune / instruction-tune during POC if you provide labeled summaries; that's a separate effort but sometimes necessary.
[07:07] Priya: We plan to provide a small labeled set of 200 summaries. Could Redwood run a tuning run as part of the POC?
[07:12] Maya: Yes, we can discuss fine-tune options and costs. For open models you can often get good improvements with a small supervised dataset. We'll include options in the POC proposal.
[07:23] Tom: Network topology question — if we do Dedicated in GCP europe-west1, can we ensure low north-south latency to our services?
[07:29] Jordan: Yes, Dedicated pools can be provisioned in the region and we support VPC peering or private links depending on cloud. For Private deployments we can even deploy the control plane inside your network.
[07:40] Anita: KMS integration: Do you support customer-managed keys in Hosted?
[07:43] Maya: We support BYOK patterns for certain plans and full KMS integration on Private. We'll include a security appendix with supported KMS providers and HSM options.
[07:53] Miguel: Competitors — we've looked at Anthropic and OpenAI; how do you position performance vs them?
[07:59] Maya: We focus on serving and economics rather than model R&D. With open models, you can match or exceed cost-efficiency and choose the model variant that best fits your workload. We'll show head-to-head metrics on your prompts.
[08:14] Priya: Anything we should be aware of regarding tokenization — for Spanish/Portuguese we'll see token inflation?
[08:20] Jordan: Yes, tokenization differences matter. We'll tokenize your sample corpus and show token utilization per language. That informs cost estimates.
[08:29] Lena: Ok, recap and next steps?
[08:32] Maya: Recap: Redwood will send a model perf matrix including quantized variants, Hosted vs Dedicated pricing scenarios, security pack, and KV/prefix caching runbook. You'll send sample prompt set and decision criteria. We'll schedule a POC kickoff in the week of Jan 12.
[08:46] Priya: Confirming I'll share prompts and 200 labeled summaries.
[08:49] Anita: I'll send the compliance checklist and residency constraints (we need EU data at rest).
[08:55] Tom: I'll join the POC kickoff and help with infra tweaks.
[08:58] Maya: Great. Anything else?
[09:01] Miguel: One quick note — we're also evaluating streaming responses for live UI. Any special considerations?
[09:06] Arjun: Streaming is supported; for UI we recommend token-level streaming and partial tool-call signals so the UI can update progressively. We can demo that in the next session.
[09:16] Lena: Thanks all.

[30:00] [Mid-call deeper fragment — technical question about sequence length tradeoffs and kernel selection]
[30:05] Jordan: On the runtime side our kernel selector picks optimized kernels based on model arch and sequence length. For long sequences it may choose different attention kernels to keep memory in check. This impacts latency and throughput, and we'll show that in the benchmark.
[30:22] Tom: Does Redwood support custom compilation flags for a model we bring?
[30:26] Arjun: For Dedicated/Private we can accept build artifacts and tune kernel flags; for Hosted we manage compilation but take requests for special builds.

[44:00] [Late call wrap-up notes]
[44:05] Maya: We'll put the POC proposal in writing and include deadlines for deliverables.
[44:12] Priya: Good, thanks.
[51:20] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials.
[51:30] Meeting end.
